description: On loan from the National Naval Aviation Museum Pensacola; the museum describes it as number 337 of 638 A4D-2N aircraft built at El Segundo which is consistent with BuNo 148491 falling inside the A4D-2N block 148435 to 148612; wears markings WE-11 and previously 006

One of the last A-6E aircraft built with under 1600 hours total time; flown to the museum from the Naval Strike Warfare Center Fallon Nevada on 12 September 1995 and prepared for display by a VA-128 crew from NAS Whidbey Island; BuNo not published

Obtained in 1992 by airshow pilot Bill Reesman of Aurora Oregon and flown as MiG Magic; suffered a ruptured fuel line and serious in-flight fire during an afterburner climb over Aurora Airport on 1 March 1994 after which the pilot landed it; Chinese licence built MiG-17; serial and registration not established
Flown by Major General Marion Carl; registration not established
Replica built by Patrick Henry; FAA registration cancelled 1 March 2018 with the museum as last registrant which is consistent with museum ownership
FAA registration cancelled 1 March 2018 with the museum as last registrant
Replica of a Mitsubishi A6M2 Model 21 built by Bill Coffey; FAA registration cancelled 6 May 2015 with the museum as last registrant
